title: Build a stock bot in one comment and I'll run it live with $50k paper money until Christmas
author: TheObserverDev
selftext:
**Reply with this** (or just write **Safe**, **Balanced** or **Wild**):

    Name: Moon Hunter
    Stocks: 20
    Min score: 80
    Price grade: B
    Sell if drops: 25%
    Max per industry: 25%
    Anything else: (describe it in your own words)

* **Stocks:** 5 to 100. 10 = bold, 50 = spread out.
* **Min score:** an AI grades every earnings report 0-100. Most picks score 70-90. 80+ = strong report. Above 90 only a few stocks qualify.
* **Price grade:** A = bargain, F = very expensive for what the company earns. B or C recommended, but you can go lower.
* **Sell if drops:** sell when a stock falls this much from its best price, or "never" to hold through anything.
* **Max per industry:** caps how much rides on one industry (tech, energy, banks...).
* **Anything else:** describe how you want your bot to behave. I'll do my best to build it.

**How it works:**

* It's **live, not a backtest**. Your bot starts on the next market day with $50k paper money. No real money.
* It **trades once a day at the closing price**, following your rules. No day trading.
* Claude (AI) reads the replies and builds each bot. I check every one before it starts.
* Your bot races everyone else's (some are mine) and the S&P 500. **I'll post the standings here every week** until Dec 31.

replies.author: TheObserverDev
replies.body: >got it! YOLO is built: 20 stocks, score 75+, grade B or better, sells at -30%, max 25% per industry. starts trading tomorrow with $50k, I’ll post standings here every week 🚀

comments.author: QATSAlgo
comments.body: QATS team here. One useful control for this paper experiment would be a bot with the same universe, number of holdings and rebalance schedule that ignores the AI score. Also pin down the close-price assumption: can the report/score used for a decision actually be known before that day’s execution cutoff? A leaderboard with turnover, drawdown and costs alongside return would be much easier to interpret. Will all bot definitions and failed/discontinued bots remain in the weekly record?

replies.author: TheObserverDev
replies.body:
good questions, thanks.

1. yes, that control is going live this week: same universe, same number of holdings and same sell rules, but it ranks purely by 1-year price gain and ignores the AI score. it races against an identical copy of the AI version.
2. a report can only be used starting the next market day’s close. so if a company reports Monday after the bell, the earliest a bot can act is Tuesday’s close. even pre-market reports wait a day, so no same-day look-ahead.
3. costs are in (0.05% per trade for the spread). drawdown and turnover aren’t on the board yet, fair point, I’ll add them.
4. yes, every bot runs forever with its rules locked and public, including the bad ones. retired bots keep trading under “former player”. nothing gets deleted for losing.
